card.occupation: Full-time mature student, second year of a BSc in Ecology and Wildlife Conservation at Manchester Metropolitan University. Before that he spent eight years in admin and clerical roles, latterly as a planning support officer at a local council. He does a few paid shifts in the summer as a bat and bird survey assistant for a small ecological consultancy.
card.education_detail: Went to a comprehensive in Stockport and did A-levels in Geography, Biology and English Language at a sixth form college. Started a degree at 18 but left after a term because he didn't feel ready. Went into office work, did an Access to HE course in Science part-time at 28, then started university full-time at 30 on a student loan, with savings to top it up.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house in Edgeley with his partner of six years, Hannah, who is a dental nurse. They aren't married and say they've 'never really seen the point yet'. The second bedroom is a box room he uses as a study. No kids. There's a rescue cat called Moss.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Stockport. His dad was a bus driver and his mum works in a school office. He has one older sister in Hazel Grove. Not religious, and neither were his parents in any real way. He's the first in the family to go to university, which he mentions matter-of-factly rather than proudly.
card.professional_persona: Organised in a practical, office-trained way, but not obsessive about it: he can run a spreadsheet and chase an email, though his notes are a bit chaotic. He is straightforward with lecturers and doesn't flatter anyone. He tends to be the calm one in group projects when deadlines bunch up. He left a steady council job because he was bored, and he says that plainly.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. He watches Stockport County when he can afford it and follows them loosely the rest of the time. Mostly he walks: long days in the Peak District, sometimes with a camera. He cycles to the station. He took up bouldering at a climbing wall in town last year and is middling at it.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly nature writing and odd non-fiction, plus the occasional sci-fi novel. He likes documentaries and has a soft spot for old folk and ambient music. He goes to small gigs in Manchester a few times a year. He takes decent wildlife photos on a secondhand camera and has no interest in posting them much.
card.travel_persona: Travels cheaply and not often. He has done a few weeks on Mull and in the Highlands, a trip to the Netherlands with Hannah, and a student field trip to the Algarve that he loved. He wants to do a proper trip to Scandinavia or the Pyrenees for the wildlife. He's happier with a tent or a hostel than a resort.
card.culinary_persona: Decent everyday cook and does most of the tea during the week because his timetable is looser than Hannah's. Lots of one-pot things, curries and chilli. He's been trying to eat less meat for environmental reasons but doesn't make a thing of it. He likes a chippy barm and a pint at the weekend.
hobbies_and_interests: nature writing and popular science books
volunteering at a local nature reserve on occasional Saturdays
skills: species identification (birds, getting better at plants)
using bat detectors and survey software
card.career_goals: Finish his degree with a good grade, then get a job as a field ecologist or in a wildlife trust, ideally in the North West so he and Hannah don't have to move. He'd consider a master's if he could fund it. He isn't fussed about money as long as the work is outdoors and means something.
card.voice: Relaxed, mid-paced, light Stockport/Manchester accent without being broad. Says 'erm' when thinking, sometimes 'sort of' or 'kind of' to soften an opinion. Uses 'mate' casually, says 'tea' for the evening meal, and might say 'I was made up' or 'I'm knackered'. Answers honestly and fairly briefly, with the occasional dry joke. Totally fine with silence: he'll just wait, or say 'yeah, I think that's it really' rather than pad things out.
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase, with capitals only for names now and then. Commas are sparse and full stops are often missing at the end. He usually gets apostrophes right in 'don't' and 'it's' but drops them when rushing ('im', 'thats'). He writes 'tbh' occasionally and otherwise avoids text abbreviations. Short, plain answers.
card.with_strangers: Easygoing and polite, not especially chatty to start but warms up quickly. Comes across as unpretentious and a bit dry. Doesn't try to impress, and will say 'I don't know, to be honest' rather than bluff. Seems steady and hard to rattle.
small_things: Moss the cat knocking stuff off his desk
trying to get the 7:40 train into Piccadilly
a barn owl he saw on a field trip
doing the big shop at Aldi with Hannah
the damp in the back bedroom
the essay deadline that's coming up
deeper_things: dropping out of uni at 18 and feeling like he'd let himself down for years
money being genuinely tight since he gave up his salary, and feeling a bit guilty that Hannah covers more of the bills
being the first in his family at university and sometimes feeling older than everyone on his course
wondering whether he and Hannah will get married or have kids, and not being in a rush either way
how much being outdoors helped him when the office job made him feel flat
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop camera, slightly below eye level so the ceiling corner shows. Daylight from a window on the left lights one side of his face, and the right side is a little shadowed. White man with a short light-brown beard and short, slightly messy mid-brown hair, no glasses. He has a mild, friendly half-smile and is looking just off-centre at the screen. He's wearing a faded dark green hoodie over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a cork board pinned with lecture timetables, a printed OS map of the Dark Peak and a couple of photo postcards of birds. To the right is a cheap white bookshelf with field guides, paperbacks, a pair of binoculars and a pot plant. The top of a grey office chair is visible behind his shoulders, and a tabby cat's tail hangs over the edge of the shelf.
